overview: This is a 'rule,' a House resolution that sets the terms for debating other bills. It lets the House take up four bills on the District of Columbia's criminal justice system, including measures on youth offender status, trying 14-year-olds as adults for certain crimes, police vehicle chases, and ending D.C.'s Judicial Nomination Commission, plus three energy bills on power grid hookups, a National Coal Council, and permits for cross-border oil, gas and power lines. For each bill it limits debate to one hour, blocks floor amendments, and allows one motion to send the bill back to committee. It also tells the House clerk to attach an earlier House-passed bill limiting a central bank digital currency to a digital asset bill, and extends several earlier House orders through March 31, 2026. One of those changes turns off, through March 31, 2026, the normal fast-track procedure for a vote on ending the national emergency the President declared on July 30, 2025. The House adopted it on September 16, 2025, and on March 25, 2026, it was amended by a later resolution, H.Res. 1131.
for: Supporters say the rule lets the House move efficiently on a package of crime and energy bills that had already been through committee, with set debate time for both sides.
against: Critics say it bundles unrelated matters, blocks amendments from the floor, and uses a procedural rule to sidestep a quick House vote on ending a presidential national emergency.
